study: MNQ New York open: movement, recovery, and continuation
type: Descriptive historical event study; no trading-strategy or holdout claim
hypothesis: An opening directional push may retrace toward the cash opening price within one or two hours; compare this with additional same-direction extension and clean continuation.
primary_sample: Common sessions with every 1-minute bar present from 09:30 inclusive through 11:45 exclusive; no contract change in that window. No filling missing bars.
initial_metrics: range and displacement in basis points
signal_definition: O=09:30 open, E=last completed opening-window close, s=sign(E-O), A=abs(E-O). Future bars start at the checkpoint; flat openings excluded only from directional outcomes.

outcomes.first_passage: First full retracement versus first equal-size extension, with future bar open checked before intrabar extremes; unresolved same-minute order labeled ambiguous
outcomes.clean_continuation: Reach equal-size extension, never retrace half the initial displacement, and finish beyond E in the initial direction

subgroups.directional_push: A >= 20 index points AND A/(opening high-low) >= 0.60; descriptive filter, not optimized

uncertainty: Headline 95% pointwise percentile intervals from 2000 seeded calendar-month cluster bootstrap samples; overlapping windows and subgroups are not independent trials; no multiplicity adjustment.
risk: Report full-horizon adverse/favorable excursion for a hypothetical fade and lower/upper bounds on adverse excursion before first return. Prices are not executable trade results; no fees, slippage, stops or fill assumptions.
decision: No profit-based pass/fail, parameter optimization, or stage promotion. Assess only historical frequencies and movement distributions; a separate specified causal trade backtest would be needed for an expectancy conclusion.
